newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on harvest pressure.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on harvest pressure.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower following a mixed session as seasonal harvest pressure outweighed spillover support from soyoil and strong export inspections data, traders said.
"We tried to rally on the very healthy bean exports but it couldn't hold. There's follow-through technical weakness from Friday," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
USDA Monday said 27.383 million bushels of soybeans were inspected for export during the week ended October 17.
That tally was well above the 10.652 million inspected the previous week.
Hedge pressure was also noted Monday as farmers concluded an active harvest weekend. Light commercial selling was reported and traders suggested the trades were linked to hedging.
Cargill, ADM, Continental Grain and Produce Grain were all said to be sellers of the January.
Traders discounted ideas farmer selling was slow, noting cash basis levels had not increased last week despite record exports and very high soybean crush levels.
But harvest was expected to grind to a halt this week as two major storm systems moved across the U.S. Midwest.
Showers were forecast for the western and central U.S. corn belt Monday night and Tuesday.
Soybeans ended 1-1/2 to 5-1/2 cents per bushel lower with November down 1-1/2 at $6.80-1/2.

Short term technical indicators show November was oversold with the nine day relative strength index (RSI) as of 1315 CDT at 15.657 points. In general the market views an RSI of 20 or less as very oversold.

Traders expected the USDA weekly crop briefs slated for release late Monday to show U.S soybean harvest at 60 to 65 percent complete as of Sunday. Forty percent of the crop had been combined as of Sunday October 15, USDA said last week.
Volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, CBOT reported.
